span: Provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of the law or by reappreciation of evidence.
why: Quotes s.34(2A) and its proviso while explaining the patent-illegality ground; the passage is statutory text and background on the amendment.

span: whether such interim award can then be set aside under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
why: Issue is whether an interim award on limitation can be challenged; not erroneous interpretation.

span: preliminary orders of condonation of delay, which do not in any way impact the arbitral award
why: Concerns which orders are appealable, not the grounds for setting aside an award.

span: or the construction of the contract is such that no fair or reasonable person would take
why: Headnote: patent illegality covers a contract construction no reasonable person would adopt, so only an unreasonable (not merely erroneous) interpretation is a ground.

span: a mere erroneous application of the law or wrong appreciation of evidence by itself is not a ground to set aside an award
why: Court's own conclusion from the precedents: erroneous application of law alone does not justify setting aside under s.34.

span: erroneous application of law cannot be categorised as patent illegality
why: Court relies on the Delhi Airport Metro principles and applies them: error of law is not patent illegality; only an interpretation no fair-minded person would adopt qualifies.

span: The High Court held that the interpretation of the terms of the contract by the Arbitral Tribunal is erroneous
why: Reports the High Court's reasoning in the lower proceedings; the Supreme Court's ruling comes later.
